answer.question: What is the data analyst internship at Icanio Tech School?
answer.answer: It is a hands-on program where students learn to turn raw business data into decisions. You move through four phases: Excel and data basics, SQL querying, Python with Pandas, and Power BI or Tableau dashboards. A practising Icanio mentor reviews your work, you build four business reports, and you earn a certificate. Durations run from 15 days to six months.

sections.heading: What a data analyst does and why companies need one
paragraphs: A data analyst answers business questions with evidence. Which product sold best last quarter? Why did customers stop renewing? Which region needs more stock next month? The analyst collects the data, cleans it, finds the pattern and explains it in plain language to the people who decide.

Every company now stores sales, customer, website and operations data. Very few people inside those companies can read it well. That gap is why analyst roles appear in banks, retail chains, hospitals, logistics firms, startups and IT services companies alike. It is also why the role suits students from commerce, science and engineering backgrounds.

A data analyst internship is the fastest way to prove you can do this work. Employers rarely hire analysts on marks alone. They want to see a cleaned dataset, a clear SQL query and a dashboard that tells a story. Our data analyst internship is built to give you exactly that proof.
bullets: Clean messy data and fix missing or duplicate values
Query databases with SQL to answer specific questions
Explore and test patterns with Python and statistics
Present findings as dashboards and short written reports

sections.heading: Who can join the data analyst internship
sections.intro: You do not need a computer science degree. You need curiosity about numbers and the patience to check your work. These four groups do especially well in our data analyst internship.

items.title: Business and commerce graduates
items.body: B.Com, BBA and MBA students who already understand sales and profit, and now want the analytical tools that make those skills far more valuable.

items.title: Everyday Excel users
items.body: Students or professionals who are comfortable with spreadsheets and want to step up to SQL, Python and BI dashboards without starting from zero.

items.title: Computer science students
items.body: B.E., B.Tech, B.Sc. and BCA students who can code and want to explore analyst roles, where business sense matters as much as syntax.

items.title: Career switchers
items.body: People from operations, accounts, teaching or support roles who want to move into data-driven work and need a structured, mentored path.

sections.heading: Data analyst internship curriculum in 4 phases
sections.intro: Each phase of the data analyst internship builds on the last. You finish every phase with a small deliverable that your mentor reviews before you move on. Shorter internships cover the early phases in depth. Longer ones complete all four and the capstone.

items.label: Phase 1
items.title: Data fundamentals and Excel
points: Data types, variables and how an analyst frames a question
PivotTables, VLOOKUP and simple macros for repeat tasks
Cleaning data: missing values, duplicates and wrong formats
Descriptive statistics: mean, median, spread and outliers
How databases and data warehouses store business data

items.label: Phase 2
items.title: SQL and database querying
points: SELECT, WHERE and JOIN across related tables
Subqueries and window functions for rankings and running totals
Aggregation with GROUP BY to summarise sales and customers
Writing efficient queries that answer a real business request
Google BigQuery basics for large, cloud-hosted datasets

items.label: Phase 3
items.title: Python for data analysis
points: Python with Pandas and NumPy for tables and calculations
Wrangling and reshaping data from several sources
Exploratory data analysis to find trends and anomalies
Charts and visualisation workflows in Jupyter Notebook
Statistical testing and A/B analysis for experiments

items.label: Phase 4
items.title: BI dashboards and career preparation
points: Interactive dashboards in Power BI and Tableau
Connecting live data sources so reports refresh on their own
Data storytelling: turning numbers into a clear recommendation
A business analytics capstone project, reviewed by your mentor
Resume building and interview practice for analyst roles

sections.intro: By the end of the data analyst internship you have skills and a body of work. Each outcome below maps to something you can show in an interview.

items.title: SQL fluency

items.title: BI dashboard expertise

items.title: Data storytelling
items.body: You present insights as a short narrative with one clear recommendation, which is the skill hiring managers test most often.

sections.heading: A typical day in the data analyst internship
paragraphs: Most days in the data analyst internship start with a short stand-up. You tell your mentor what you finished yesterday, what you plan today and where you are stuck. This is the same rhythm our delivery teams follow at Icanio Technologies.

The core of the day is hands-on work on a dataset. One week you might clean three months of order data in Excel. The next week you might write SQL to find the customers who stopped buying. Later you build a Power BI page that shows the trend in one glance.

Late afternoon is review time. Your mentor reads your query, checks your chart and asks the question a manager would ask. In our experience, this daily review is what separates a data analyst internship that builds real skill from a course that only covers theory.
bullets: Hands-on work on a real business dataset
Written notes in Jupyter or Google Sheets for every analysis
End-of-day review of queries, charts and conclusions

faqs.q: Do I need coding experience for the data analyst internship?
faqs.a: No. We start with Excel and data thinking, then introduce SQL and Python step by step. Many interns write their first line of code during the program. What helps most is comfort with numbers and a habit of double-checking results. Your mentor sets the pace to match your background.

faqs.q: Is this data analyst internship suitable for commerce students?
faqs.a: Yes. B.Com, BBA and MBA students often do very well because they already understand sales, margins and customers. The data analyst internship adds the tools to prove those insights with data. Many commerce interns find SQL easier than they expected once they see it applied to business questions.

faqs.q: How long is the data analyst internship?
faqs.a: You choose the duration, from 15 days up to six months. A short internship covers Excel and SQL in depth with one report. Three to six months lets you complete all four phases, the Python work, the dashboards and the full capstone project. Our team helps you decide based on your goals.

faqs.q: Which tools will I learn during the internship?
faqs.a: You work with Microsoft Excel, Google Sheets, MySQL, Google BigQuery, Python with Pandas and NumPy, Jupyter Notebook, Power BI and Tableau. These cover the full analyst workflow: collecting data, cleaning it, querying it, exploring it and presenting it. You use each tool on real tasks rather than just watching demos.

faqs.q: Can I do the data analyst internship online?
faqs.a: Yes. You can attend offline at our centre, join online, or choose part-time weekday or weekend batches. Hybrid is also possible. Online interns get the same 1:1 mentorship, dataset reviews and certificate as offline interns, so pick whatever fits your college timetable.

faqs.q: What projects will I build in the internship?
faqs.a: You build four business reports: a sales analysis, a customer insights study and executive dashboards, followed by a capstone project. The capstone takes one business problem from raw data to a recommendation. Together they form a portfolio that shows employers how you think, not only which tools you know.

faqs.q: Will I get a certificate and placement support?
faqs.a: Every intern who completes the data analyst internship receives an Icanio Tech School certificate stating the track and duration. Phase 4 includes resume building and interview practice. Top performers are referred to the Icanio Technologies talent team, and our wider programs have placed over 1,000 students.

faqs.q: What is the difference between data analyst and business analyst?
faqs.a: A data analyst works mainly with numbers: querying, cleaning and visualising data to answer questions. A business analyst works mainly with people and processes: gathering requirements and shaping solutions. The skills overlap. If you enjoy the business side, look at our business analyst internship as well.

takeaways: The data analyst internship covers Excel, SQL, Python and BI dashboards in four mentored phases.
